newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on calm pre-FOMC trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on calm pre-FOMC trade.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates modified earlier increases to close up 40 basis points at 21.40 percent on Tuesday after what traders described as a quiet session.
"The market still welcomes falling primary rates, so secondary rates have held steady for several sessions now,' a trader said.
Dealers added that secondary rates were also stable, because the peso remained stable despite falls in primary rates on Monday night.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 0.2 of a peso softer at 7.8220/7.8270 per dollar.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 25 basis points at 22.90 percent.
Dealers said trade was quiet while the market awaited the outcome on Wednesday of the Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates.
Dealers saw as a good omen for the FOMC meeting the late fall in U.S. long bond yields, to 6.71 percent from an early 6.75 percent.
Banco de Mexico drained surplus liquidity of 2.443 billion pesos through four auctions to purchase paper.
Traders had originally expected a liquidity shortfall, due to credit maturities and demand for cash prior to Wednesday's holiday, but government spending created a surplus.

Liquidity of 1.038 billion pesos was scheduled to flow back into the market on Thursday, but an oversupply of 1.642 billion pesos of paper carried over from the auction was expected to tighten liquidity.
Mexican financial markets will be closed on Wednesday for Constitution Day. ((--Patricia Lezama, Mexico City newsroom +525 728-9554))
